result:
What I'd do next: no actions. I'd reply with one question.

---

Thanks for the spreadsheet description. It already tells me a lot. Seed, Packets, Borrower, Date out, Date back is a sensible core. The interesting part is that about a third of the "Date back" cells are empty.

Seed libraries are unusual because "coming back" often doesn't mean the same packet returns. It usually means someone grows the plants and brings back seed they saved, sometimes a season or a year later, sometimes from a different variety, and sometimes never. So those empty cells could mean several different things. People might still be growing. The seed might never have been expected back. Or returns might be happening without anyone writing them down. Each of those leads to a different tool. One fix is reminders to borrowers. Another is easier logging at the table. A third is tracking saved-seed donations as their own thing.

When you look at those blank "Date back" cells, what do you think is actually going on with most of them, and what problem is that causing for the garden?
